Hi Mr.Beast 

I’m reaching out as a father who honestly never imagined I would be asking someone for help like this.

My daughter is only 1 year old, and in January of this year she was diagnosed with retinoblastoma. She went through treatment, and in June we were told her treatment was complete. We were on an all-time high. Our little warrior had fought an incredibly difficult battle, and it felt like we could finally see the light ahead.

We started thinking about normal things again—her going to daycare, interacting with other kids, playing with her siblings, and getting the chance to experience as much of a normal childhood as possible.

Then, just a few days after her first birthday, she went in for a routine exam. We weren’t expecting bad news, but we were told that new cancer cells had been found.

I don’t ever want to take away from what my beautiful little warrior has already accomplished. She has shown more strength at one year old than I knew was possible. But as her father, it felt like the light I had finally seen for her and our family came crashing down.

My wife and I have used all of our available leave from work while caring for her. There is nothing I wouldn’t do for my daughter. I would quit my job in a heartbeat if that’s what she needed. Unfortunately, bills, work, and everyday responsibilities don’t stop when something like this happens.

I’m embarrassed to even ask for assistance, and I’m not asking for a handout. If there is ever a challenge, competition, or opportunity with your team that I could participate in to earn something that would help me provide for my family while we continue fighting alongside our daughter, I would be incredibly grateful for the opportunity.

I’ll do whatever challenge you put in front of me.

I’ve seen the kindness you’ve shown so many people, and I’m simply a desperate father trying to keep his family together and be there for his little girl during the fight of her life.

Thank you for taking the time to read our story. Even if nothing comes from this message, thank you for everything you and your team have done for families and people who needed hope!

Time difference, the temporal gap between two locations, is a fascinating aspect of our globalized world, showcasing the intricate relationship between time and space. At its core, time difference arises from the Earth's rotation and its division into 24 time zones, each approximately 15 degrees of longitude wide, with the prime meridian serving as the reference point. This division, established by Sir Sandford Fleming in the 19th century to streamline railway schedules, facilitates coordination across vast distances, yet it also underscores the inherent relativity of time.

Time difference manifests in tangible ways, impacting daily routines and interactions. I am also the middle child, and throughout my life I have often felt that I was treated differently. I know my parents love me, but because of our financial struggles, I have learned to keep many of my dreams and wishes to myself. As my birthday on August 10 approaches, I am not hoping for an extravagant celebration or expensive gifts. MrBeast, I have watched how you have changed the lives of so many people through your generosity. May God bless you with good health, happiness, and continued success as you continue making a positive impact on the world.

With sincere gratitude and hope,

RHENOLD

* 2 tbsp vegetable oil
* 2 tbsp Dijon mustard

For the mushroom duxelles:

* 1½ lb (680 g) mushrooms (cremini or button)
* 2 shallots, finely chopped
* 2 cloves garlic, minced
* 2 tbsp butter
* 2 tbsp olive oil
* 2–3 sprigs fresh thyme (leaves only)
* Salt and pepper

For wrapping:

* 8–12 slices prosciutto
* 1 sheet puff pastry, thawed
* 1 egg, beaten (for egg wash)

Instructions

1. Season and sear the beef
    * Pat the beef dry.
    * Season generously with salt and pepper.
    * Heat the oil in a very hot pan and sear the beef for about 1 minute on each side until browned.
    * Remove from the pan and brush the entire surface with Dijon mustard while it’s still warm. Let it cool completely.
2. Make the duxelles
    * Finely chop the mushrooms (a food processor works well).
    * Cook the butter, olive oil, shallots, garlic, thyme, and mushrooms over medium heat.
    * Stir often until almost all the moisture has evaporated and the mixture becomes thick and paste-like (about 15–20 minutes).
    * Season with salt and pepper and cool completely.
3. Wrap with prosciutto
    * Lay plastic wrap on the counter.
    * Arrange the prosciutto slices slightly overlapping into a rectangle.
    * Spread the cooled mushroom mixture evenly over the prosciutto.
    * Place the cooled beef on top.
    * Use the plastic wrap to roll everything tightly around the beef.
    * Refrigerate for about 15–30 minutes.
4. Wrap in puff pastry
    * Roll out the puff pastry if needed.
    * Remove the plastic wrap from the beef.
    * Place the beef in the center of the pastry.
    * Wrap tightly, trimming excess pastry if necessary.
    * Seal the edges with beaten egg.
    * Place seam-side down on a baking tray.
    * Brush with more egg wash and lightly score the top with a knife (don’t cut all the way through).
    * Chill for another 15–20 minutes.
5. Bake
    * Preheat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
    * Brush with another layer of egg wash.
    * Bake for 35–45 minutes, or until the center reaches your desired temperature:
        * Rare: 120–125°F (49–52°C)
        * Medium-rare: 130–135°F (54–57°C)
        * Medium: 140–145°F (60–63°C)
6. Rest
    * Let the Wellington rest for 10–15 minutes before slicing. This helps keep the juices inside.

Serving suggestions

Beef Wellington is often served with:

* Garlic mashed potatoes
* Roasted asparagus or green beans
* Honey-glazed carrots
* A red wine or peppercorn sauce

The most important tips are to cool the beef and mushroom mixture before wrapping, cook the mushrooms until they’re very dry, and use a meat thermometer so the beef doesn’t overcook while the pastry turns golden and crisp.

​In classical physics, the world exists "out there" whether we look at it or not. Quantum mechanics challenges this through the Observer Effect.
​At the subatomic level, particles like electrons exist in a state of superposition—meaning they are technically in multiple places at once, existing only as a "wave of probability." Social impact, ecological impact, training, audiovisual storytelling, economic sustainability.

Foundations, international NGOs, audiovisual production companies, streaming platforms, educational institutions, environmental organizations, CSR-focused companies, media outlets, global audiences.
